findings.passage: He has referred on the record to "my wife," "my son" and "my daughter."
findings.problem: The quotation "my wife" is not Sankar's. The only "my wife" in any opened source is in the Meta conversation (S14, 45:23), and the speaker is the host, Andrew Bosworth. Sankar's answer about his production company runs from 44:15 to 45:18 and ends "for our children, like I want them to see movies with heroes that are real heroes"; the host then replies "That's right. Yeah, I agree with you so strongly on that. And I'm a huge movie buff. My wife and I kind of go every week to catch a film on date night"; Sankar resumes at 46:00. A search of every saved caption track and every re-fetched text found no first-person reference by Sankar to a wife. The evidence record repeats the error (C34; S14 context: 'Source for "my wife" and "my son" in his own voice'). The underlying fact is supported another way: Joe Lonsdale introduces him on camera as "a husband and a father" (S07, 05:29) and he answers without correcting it, and "my son" and "my daughter" are his own words (S16, 01:31:08, caption-only).
findings.acceptance_test: The marriage FAQ no longer attributes "my wife" to Sankar. Its "Yes" rests on what is sourced (for example Lonsdale's on-camera "a husband and a father", said to him, plus his own "my son" and "my daughter"). The sentence about not naming his wife or counting his children stays. C34 and the S14 context note are corrected.

findings.passage: we have to sue the army to compete at some point.
findings.problem: Misquotation by one word that changes the tense. The YouTube original-language caption track (S08, 09:30) reads "You know we had to sue the army to compete at some point", and an independent Whisper medium.en transcription of the saved audio made for this verification reads "You know, we had to sue the army to compete at some point." Only the research stage's small.en pass gives "have". "Had" is also the reading that fits the 2016 lawsuit the next paragraph describes. The article prints the disputed word inside quotation marks, in the Type 8 argument.
findings.acceptance_test: The quotation reads "we had to sue the army to compete at some point", or is cut back to words both transcriptions share. C147's claim and passage match the article.

findings.passage: No telling of the family story from before his public turn was found either; the earliest opened is from December 2024.
findings.problem: An opened source in the evidence record contradicts this. In the ARK Invest interview posted September 28, 2023 (S15, 01:57 to 02:13, original-language captions) he says he came to Palantir "because of the mission", that he grew up "as a child essentially of refugees", that "we fled violence in Nigeria", and that he was "raised with the immense gratitude of understanding the counterfactual every single day of how lucky I was to be in this country". That is the gratitude-and-counterfactual account thirteen months before "The Defense Reformation". The record's S15 context note ("no family material") and C177 are wrong, and the fix accepted for future-04 rests on them. The same error colours "Sankar has been repeating it since at least December 2024" and "the night he has described in interviews since December 2024": those dates hold for the "dead in a ditch in Lagos" sentence and the robbery details, but the frame is documented from 2023. The article names this absence as part of why confidence stays at medium, so the reader is given a weaker record than the one opened.
findings.acceptance_test: The limits section and C177 say that a telling from September 2023, before the October 2024 public turn, was found, attributed to the ARK Invest interview with its date and paraphrased or checked by ear (the wording is caption-only). The text says what that telling contains (refugees, fleeing violence in Nigeria, gratitude, "the counterfactual") and what it does not (the robbery details and the "dead in a ditch in Lagos" sentence, whose earliest opened instance remains December 2024). The S15 context note is corrected. Confidence is not raised on this alone.

findings.passage: Four things on record lean Six, and none of them settles it.
findings.problem: Scored against the standard's Enneagram anchors, the type argument is honest and seriously tested but stops short of the release floor for a standard profile. By the article's own account no observation separates a bold Six from a loyal Eight ("none of them settles it"; "the record is empty"), no costly choice is shown that the Six motive explains better than pay or position ("None of these deferrals cost him anything"; "Loyalty and money point the same way"), and Types 1 and 3 are both left live. The material in the record that a loyal-Eight reading predicts least is on the page but is not used in the 6-versus-8 test: his own rule that a heretic needs "protection from the top", the "rabbi ... guru ... parole officer" description of Karp, and a gratitude account that predates the public campaign (verify-03). This is a limit of the argument as built on this record, not a wording slip.
findings.acceptance_test: Either the 6-versus-8 test names at least one sourced observation that the loyal-Eight reading cannot comfortably accommodate and says why, using material already sourced, with every stated limit kept and confidence still medium; or, if no such observation survives, the profile is held as insufficient_evidence with the non-ally testimony task. No sentence claims more certainty than the record holds, and the type and its rival do not change without a refreshed expanded review.

findings.passage: the Hudson Institute's page for the dinner calls him a trustee
findings.problem: The Hudson event page, reopened on 2026-10-13, lists him as "Former Trustee" and says "Shyam Sankar was a trustee at Hudson Institute"; the Hudson expert page says the same. The page does not call him a trustee in the present tense. The allied-venue point survives.
findings.acceptance_test: The sentence says the page calls him a former trustee (or that he was a Hudson trustee), and C175 matches.

findings.passage: In the same answer he says heretics require two things: room for the heresy, and some protection from the top.
findings.problem: It is his next answer, not the same one. In S07 the sacrifice remark ends at 27:12, Lonsdale then asks why the bureaucracy keeps trying to kill heretics, and Sankar's reply ("that question you just asked is why I wrote the book ... heretics require two things") begins at 27:28. Captions and an independent Whisper pass agree.
findings.acceptance_test: The sentence places the two requirements in his next answer or in the same exchange, not in the same answer.

findings.passage: a colleague read his harshest critique as "what I owe you all."
findings.problem: Metadata drifts from the body and the source. Mabrey describes receiving "a Shyam Bomb" at the Toronto airport; nothing in Colossus calls it his harshest, and the body says only "a Shyam Bomb". The same FAQ gives "dictator" as his word for "how he runs his part of the company", where the body and the sources limit it to the seam between forward deployed engineering and product ("owning that almost as a dictator").
findings.acceptance_test: The Type 8 FAQ says what the body says: a colleague read one of his company-wide critiques as "what I owe you all", and "dictator" is his word for how he runs the seam between the field engineers and the product team.

findings.passage: The 2010 lawsuit would count too, if its allegation were accurate.
findings.problem: Forward reference with no antecedent. At this point the reader has met only the 2016 Army lawsuit; the i2 case is not introduced until "What the record cannot show", five sections later. A first-time reader cannot tell which lawsuit or which allegation is meant.
findings.acceptance_test: The sentence identifies the case in a clause (for example, a 2010 suit by a competitor that named him personally, covered below) or moves next to the paragraph that introduces it.

findings.passage: No source opened for this page names his birth city.
findings.problem: Literally untrue of the evidence record. S29, an opened source, says he "was born in Mumbai in the early 1980s" (reconfirmed live on 2026-10-13). The record sets it aside, rightly, as an unsourced newsletter that tracks the Colossus profile, but the FAQ says no opened source names a city. The age FAQ uses the accurate form ("No reliable source").
findings.acceptance_test: The parents FAQ says no reliable or sourced account names his birth city, or says that the one unsourced claim found (Mumbai) is not relied on. C113 matches.
